tier_reason: Public artifact harness (bench/ built into ./build/bssl_bench, run via reproduce.sh; OpenSSL baseline harness in kevin-he-01/vroom-openssl) benchmarks VROOM against BoringSSL BN_mod_mul_montgomery, FLINT 3.2.1 and OpenSSL, with compiler (Clang 21.1.8), flags (CMake Release -O3 plus -mavx512f -mavx512ifma in CMakeLists.txt) and CPU (Xeon Platinum 8488C) all stated; the results are in a peer-reviewed USENIX Security 2026 paper. The repo itself prints no numbers; the headline figures were seen only in a WebSearch summary of the paper abstract because eprint.iacr.org and usenix.org are blocked here.

corrections.claimed_speedup: The repository README gives no figures; it says 'the relative speedup of VROOM over each baseline is the paper's claim' and points to the paper (IACR ePrint 2026/393). A WebSearch result summarizing the paper abstract (the ePrint and USENIX pages themselves could not be opened, egress blocked) states that VROOM accelerates RSA-4096 signatures by 4.0x (verify) and 1.3x (sign) over OpenSSL, and BLS signature verification by 3.43x over the assembly-optimized BLST library (the BLS result is not covered by this repository). These figures are not verified from an opened page.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Clang 21.1.8 (official LLVM prebuilt, installed by install_deps.sh); configure.sh runs 'cmake -GNinja -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release'; CMakeLists.txt adds -O3 to the Release flags and -mavx512f -mavx512ifma for the RNS path; FLINT 3.2.1; runs pinned with 'taskset -c 0 ./build/bssl_bench'
corrections.baseline: BoringSSL BN_mod_mul_montgomery / BN modular exponentiation and RSA (same binary, multiplication backend swapped), OpenSSL at commit 7a53925 including its AVX-512 IFMA almost-Montgomery routines ossl_rsaz_amm52x{20,30,40} (separate harness kevin-he-01/vroom-openssl), FLINT 3.2.1 (GMP-based mpn_mod_mul / fmpz_mod_mul), and Arkworks (Rust, modmul only)
corrections.stars_or_usage: 8 stars, 1 fork, 11 commits; artifact repository for the USENIX Security 2026 paper by Langowski, He and Devadas (MIT)
corrections.caveats: The README warns that this is a research prototype, 'not a production-ready library', tested only on random inputs to select functions, and that it may contain memory leaks, memory errors and other (security) bugs; commit 616817a (2026-05-22) is titled 'Fix buffer overflow in several files'. No speedup figures appear in the repository; the headline numbers come from the paper abstract and were only seen in a search summary here. The VROOM code itself uses only BoringSSL BN_* routines (no GMP/FLINT). OpenSSL and Arkworks columns come from separate harnesses (baselines/openssl submodule, baselines/arkworks). FLINT is the GMP-based baseline, not GMP itself. Requires AVX-512 IFMA (Sapphire Rapids class CPU). Fork of BoringSSL commit 3fb010b, licensed Apache-2.0. The GPU and elliptic-curve/pairing results of the paper live in other repositories not covered here.

notes: Harness, flags and CPU check out; eprint.iacr.org, usenix.org, kevin-he-01.github.io and api.semanticscholar.org were all egress-blocked, so the paper's tables were not read and the 4.0x/1.3x RSA-4096 figures rest on a WebSearch abstract summary; re-check from the PDF on an unrestricted machine. Record the research-prototype security warning and the buffer-overflow fix as shortcomings.

tier_reason: The README repeats the peer-reviewed FCCM'22 result (2.0 GMAC/s of 512-bit GEMM on an Alveo U250, an order of magnitude above a 36-core dual-socket Xeon node, 375x CPU cores); the repository only times the FPGA side (host/Microbenchmark.cpp, host/TestMatrixMultiplication.cpp) and uses MPFR as an untimed correctness reference, and the CPU model, compiler and flags of the baseline are not in the repo, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 2.0 GMAC/s of 512-bit matrix-matrix multiplication on an Alveo U250, 'an order of magnitude higher than a 36-core dual-socket Xeon node, corresponding to 375x CPU cores worth of throughput'. The FCCM'22 abstract, seen only in WebSearch summaries (arXiv 2204.06256, spcl.inf.ethz.ch and ar5iv were blocked), reports versus MPFR on that node: 9.8x at 4.8 GOp/s for 512-bit multiplication, 5.3x at 1.2 GOp/s for 1024-bit multiplication (more than 351x and 191x CPU cores), and 10x at 2.0 GOp/s for matrix multiplication.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 41 stars, 7 forks, 153 commits; peer-reviewed at FCCM 2022 (ETH Zurich SPCL)
corrections.caveats: No LICENSE file (LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt and COPYING all 404; none shown on the GitHub page), so the code is reference only. Hardware design for Xilinx XRT FPGAs (Vitis HLS), not a CPU library. The README does not name MPFR; the repo builds with MPFR semantics by default (APFP_SEMANTICS=MPFR) and uses mpfr_mul only as an untimed correctness reference (host/MatrixMultiplicationReference.cpp), so the CPU-baseline harness is not public. The MPFR speedup figures come from the paper abstract, seen only in search summaries because arXiv and the SPCL host were blocked. FPGA board versus a whole 36-core CPU node, not an equal-silicon comparison; CPU model, compiler and MPFR version are not in the README. Last commit 2022-05-17, more than 3 years old.

notes: README numbers match the record; the paper (arXiv 2204.06256) was unreachable (arxiv.org, ar5iv, spcl.inf.ethz.ch, eupilot.eu blocked), so the MPFR ratios stay labelled as abstract-summary figures. Tier B on the strength of the FCCM'22 peer review.

tier_reason: First-party plots (bench/serial_mp_N1024_time.png, bench/parallel_mp_C4_N1024_time.png) with gcc 9.3.0 -O3, MPFR 4.1.0/GMP 6.2.1 and an i5-6500 stated, but the Mathematica and MATLAB/Advanpix baseline scripts are not in the repository (bench/ holds only PNG plots) and there is no peer review, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'a more than 2x speed-up to Mathematica and a 10x speed-up to MATLAB' (Advanpix toolbox) in serial computation with precision up to 1 million digits, and 'a 10x speed-up to MATLAB' with 4 CPU cores at high precision; no Mathematica multicore comparison. Approximate values read from the log-scale plots (derived from page data): serial at 1,048,576 digits mpFFT about 110 s versus Mathematica about 250 s and MATLAB about 1,300 s per FFT; at 16 digits mpFFT about 0.00085 s versus MATLAB about 0.0016 s and Mathematica about 0.011 s, so the MATLAB gap is only about 2x at low precision; 4 cores at 1,048,576 digits mpFFT about 36 s versus MATLAB about 380 s.
corrections.caveats: Baselines are proprietary systems (Mathematica 11.1, MATLAB 2019a with Advanpix) and the repository holds no scripts for them (bench/ contains only PNG plots), so the comparison cannot be reproduced from the repo; the speedups are first-party and read from plots. The 10x over MATLAB holds at high precision; at 16-128 digits the gap is roughly 2x. Single i5-6500 machine, 2021 versions. Source code is Apache-2.0; the README states the project content (documentation) is CC BY 4.0. Self-described as 'still in development and far from complete'; the repository has a single commit (2021-10-10). Overlaps the FFT category; kept here because it is a multiprecision (MPFR-based) FFT.

notes: README and plots match the record; last_commit 2021-10-10 is confirmed by the commits page (single 'initial commit'). Plot readings are approximate and labelled as derived.
